title: Born 1905, a lawyer and pianist, first jazz heard on records
summary: Ashcraft gives his birth year, family and law career, and says he and the Austin boys first met jazz through records such as the Friars Inn Farewell Blues.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I was born in 1905, which was approximately when most of the Austin High School band were born. I might add that I was probably born in just about the right place at about the right time for some unusual chances to observe, and I wish I'd observed a little better. Or at least I wish I'd recorded it a little better. I'm a third-generation lawyer. My family came here from Virginia and from Massachusetts and came up from Vandalia, Illinois. I have two sisters. I've been a lawyer ever since, a member of a Chicago law firm. My first connection with jazz music was approximately the same as that of the Austin boys. I think that our, I can speak for all of them in saying that the first contact we had was through records. The, we had very little access toward anything except the original Dixieland jazz band as a jazz source, that is of a, of a, anything like a Dixieland band. And as I recall, I was depending heavily on, I was a pianist. And I think the first piano that impressed me at all was the all-star trio, Oman and Arden, later on Zez Confrey. And I was inclined to throw them all out the window the first time I had that record of Carolina Shout of James P. Johnson, which must have been in the neighborhood of the, of World War I. It was an okay record, Keep Off the Grass. It was the other side. I still have it. As far as bands were concerned, we heard lots of them, like the Happy Six, Paul Specht. But I think that the first impression that upset, this would go from a Partland, probably Freeman, certainly me. I think the first record we all heard that really made a profound impression on us was Farewell Blues by the Friars Inn band. And, this was very close to the coming of, of Bix. And Bix being a couple years older than we, which made a great deal of difference at that age, that teenage, most of us didn't really know him very well. I'm talking now about 1920, 21. I think my date would be just about right on that.
